source: one of pi's own session logs (harnager, 2026-10-30T19-51-36-153Z_01a18e5e-21d8-73b2-889d-e9a2090f107e.jsonl), cut at its first `chrome_screenshot` tool result. Chosen over the un-bien log's screenshot because that chain is 808 entries deep; this one reaches an image result at entry 44. pi's log lines are the entries the extension forwards, minus the leading `session` line.
scrub: Content → «length»; absolute paths replaced. The one thing NOT reduced to a length is the image payload: it is replaced by a VALID 1x1 PNG (the same placeholder the browser double sends), because the reference decodes `data` before it counts a card's images — base64 replaced by «116164» decodes to nothing, and BOTH implementations then report `images: 0`, which tests the decoder's rejection rather than the fold. The real payload was 116164 chars of PNG. `details` collapses to key → type name (the real one carried `path`, `width: 1024`, `height: 578`); `mimeType` is kept.
description: Images on the replay plane, captured rather than authored: a `chrome_screenshot` result whose content is `[image, text]` in that order (image FIRST, the "Screenshot 1024x578 png (42KB) saved to …" line second), with `details: {path,width,height}` and the image inline as `{type:"image", data: base64, mimeType:"image/png"}`. Pins that image blocks ride the RESULT of a tool card, not their own row — the corpus's `images` field is a per-card count, and the card's face is still `terminal` (text plus dimensions), not an image face. A client that renders images as separate transcript rows, or that makes an image result a different card kind, diverges here. Also carries a second image shape from the same source corpus: a `read` of an image FILE, content [text, image] in the OPPOSITE order (pi's caption `Read image file [image/jpeg]…` first), `details` absent (the real value was null). Order is not a property a client may assume, and a `read` card can be a card whose result is an image.
note: Pasted images do NOT arrive like this. A screenshot pasted at pi's prompt lands in the log as a user message with one `text` block holding a temp file path (`/var/folders/…/pasted-image-….png`) — no base64, no image block. To a remote client that path points at a file on the host machine. The read-of-image pair (toolCall entry + toolResult) is real — captured at entry 2060 of a harnager session — but RE-PARENTED onto this scenario's chain: 2000+ entries of ancestry would not fit in a fixture. Content, ids, toolCallId, timestamps and the owning toolCall are the captured ones; only parentId is adjusted.
